item.title: Cees Nooteboom has passed away | Literature
item.description: We just got the news that Cees Nooteboom, the Dutch novelist, poet and travel writer, has died aged 92. His publisher, De Bezige Bij, said he passed away peacefully on his beloved island of Menorca, in a statement issued on behalf of his wife, photographer Simone Sassen. Born in The Hague in 1933, Nooteboom debuted in 1955 with {Philip and the Others}, inspired by hitchhiking journeys across Scandinavia and the Mediterranean. The novel won the Anne Frank Prize and became a modern Dutch classic.

item.title: Ukraine will hold elections only after ceasefire, says Zelensky
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says elections in Ukraine will take place only once a ceasefire with Russia is secured and full security guarantees are in place, pushing back against suggestions that Washington is pressuring Kyiv to hold ballots sooner. "We will move to elections when all the necessary security guarantees are in place," Zelensky said, adding that if Russia cooperates, hostilities could end by summer. item.title: WhatsApp says Russia tried to block service to promote state-backed app
item.description: Russia attempted to "fully block" WhatsApp, Meta Platforms' messaging service, according to the company (via Reuters), in a bid to encourage users to switch to a state-backed app. This comes as Moscow promotes home-grown platforms and seeks tighter control over its internet space. The action follows previous restrictions on WhatsApp and Telegram, which Russian authorities said failed to cooperate on law enforcement requests.
